Since the two processes result in distinctly different snow and ice crystal forms during times of precipitation, and because the form of the snow and ice crystals are a clue to the physical conditions within the atmosphere at the time of crystal formation, the study will also provide evidence bearing on the properties of the atmosphere. By interrelating these various factors, it will be possible to construct models of the present atmospheric conditions which may be useful in the interpretation of the chemical data from the ice cores obtained during the RISP operation, and the relation of snow chemistry variation to paleoclimates and extent of sea ice cover around the continent. The ice core studies provide a vertical profile of atmospheric history at a point; these meteorological studies may allow those vertical profiles to be related to reconstructions of the regional conditions at any given time.
Glaciological Investigations
The field data relating to the dynamics of ice shelves are of great importance to those investigators carrying out model studies. The scarcity of "real" numbers to plug into the calculations has resulted in very gross errors in some instances.
